title: Nodes inside `SubViewport` don't capture mouse events immediately after changing `Button` `mouse_filter` to ignore/pass
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6], v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8] (Does not look like regression)

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7652) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700HQ CPU @ 2.80GHz (8 threads)

### Issue description

Nodes within a `SubViewport` which are placed below a button, doesn't capture mouse down event immediately after changing `Button` `mouse_filter` to ignore/pass. Those nodes can begin capturing mouse events only after the mouse button is released then pressed again.

However, if the node is placed outside of the `SubViewport`, then it can immediately capture mouse down event as soon as the mouse filter is changed to ignore on the button. Attaching videos of both scenario:

- When the input receiving node is placed **outside** SubViewport

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9df687c7-fa8b-4e66-aa0f-b9ae2b955e1d


- When the input receiving node is placed **inside** SubViewport

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f25cc750-6105-4c87-8f73-550f2f028fdb


### Expected Behaviour
Nodes also inside subviewport and behind buttons should be able to receive mouse input event immediately after button's mouse filter is changed to pass or ignore. 

### Steps to reproduce

In below attached MRP, you can move the `Node2D` in and out of subviewport to check for the outcome in both scenario

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[buttontest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20813265/buttontest.zip)
